title: Fix DAO transit-to-target pairing in receive_from_peer()
description: In rust/lichen-rpl/src/multi_instance.rs line 553-561, the receive_from_peer() function always uses message.transit.first() for ALL targets, ignoring any subsequent transit entries. This means if a DAO backbone message has targets=[A,B,C] with transits=[T1,T2,T3], routes will be stored as [(A,T1),(B,T1),(C,T1)] instead of the correct [(A,T1),(B,T2),(C,T3)]. Fix by pairing by index or documenting the expected 1:N relationship.
close_reason: Fixed receive_from_peer() to pair targets with transits by index using enumerate/get(i), added test to verify multi-target/multi-transit pairing
